findings.label: Vitiligo-like depigmentation
findings.evidence: extension to non-sun exposed areas demonstrating hyperpigmentation and extensive depigmentation

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a patient with HIV-associated chronic actinic dermatitis (Fitzpatrick V) showing extensive depigmentation and hyperpigmentation of the trunk, arms and hands. The caption explicitly attributes the findings to CAD and names extensive depigmentation, matching the vitiligo-like depigmentation vocabulary term; the involvement of non-sun-exposed areas and vitiligo-like depigmentation is described in the text as a severe late-stage variant rather than the classic photodistributed eczematous presentation, hence typicality 'variant'. Skin tone judged visually as dark.
panels.attribution_text: Isaacs and Lehloenya. HIV-associated photodermatitis in African populations.. Frontiers in allergy 2023. doi:10.3389/falgy.2023.1159387. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Chronic actinic dermatitis of HIV in Fitzpatrick skin type V with extension to non-sun exposed areas demonstrating hyperpigmentation and extensive depigmentation.
in_text_mentions: ibution and morphology are indistinguishable from CAD in HIV-uninfected persons. In severe cases, HIV-associated late-stage CAD may present with hypopigmented or vitiligo-like depigmentation (19,20). Figure 2 CAD in the setting of HIV seems to predominantly affect men of Fitzpatrick skin types V–VI, which is consistent with observed studies of CAD in HIV-uninfected patients. HIV-associated CAD has also been described in Fitzpatrick skin types III and IV, although less commonly. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Clinical photograph of a 72-year-old male with biopsy-proven chronic actinic dermatitis showing photodistributed lichenified erythematous plaques on the face and neck. b: H&E histology from the same patient with biopsy-proven chronic actinic dermatitis; shows dermal inflammatory infiltrate. Included as disease-specific histopathology from a human patient.

panels.figure_caption: (a, b) Hyperkeratotic, lichenified and erythematous plaques seen on photodistributed areas only (a—face, neck and b—hands).
in_text_mentions: A 72‐year‐old male presented with a 12‐year history of biopsy‐proven CAD, manifesting as eczematous, lichenified plaques in photodistributed areas (Figure 1a,b). Previous treatments, including topical and systemic steroids, oral hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, and strict sun protection, were ineffective, leading to severe disease progression. A short course of cyclosporine at 300 mg/day led to improvement; however, the patient's condition worsened when the dose was reduced to 100 mg.
